limitations_and_boundaries: Theoretical results are only available for linear-based GNNs like SGC or simple spectral graph convolution; analysis for more complex GNN architectures is left for future work.
SJLR hyperparameter optimization is challenging due to expanded search space.
Current implementation of SJLR relies on a bank of good edges to add based solely on triangles of edges with most negative curvature, so it cannot directly connect long-distance nodes.
Exploring more sophisticated curvature metrics weighted with shortest path distance would introduce high computational cost, making it impractical for large-scale graphs.

research_questions.statement: What is the relationship between over-smoothing and over-squashing in deep GNNs?

provenance.text_excerpt: Our work reveals that over-smoothing and over-squashing are intrinsically related to the spectral gap of the graph Laplacian, resulting in an inevitable trade-off between these two issues, as they cannot be alleviated simultaneously.

claims.statement: Over-smoothing and over-squashing are intrinsically related to the spectral gap of the graph Laplacian, resulting in an inevitable trade-off.

experiments_or_tasks: Theoretical derivation linking over-smoothing and over-squashing via spectral gap and Cheeger inequality.

methods.name: Spectral analysis with random walk and Cheeger inequality
methods.protocol_description: Use random walk matrix and spectral gap of normalized Laplacian to show exponential convergence to stationary distribution (over-smoothing). Connect over-squashing to spectral gap via Cheeger inequality, establishing trade-off: reducing bottlenecks (alleviating over-squashing) accelerates convergence (worsens over-smoothing), and vice versa.

study_units.name: Theoretical analysis of over-smoothing and over-squashing trade-off

provenance.text_excerpt: From Theorem 3, we have that if s→0 then h_G→∞, i.e., we can promote less “bottleneckness” in the graph if we accelerate the convergence to the stationary distribution. Similarly, if h_G→0 then s→∞, i.e., we can avoid converging to the stationary distribution if we promote a bottleneck-kind structure in the graph. In other words, we can reduce over-squashing by accelerating the convergence to the stationary distribution that worsens over-smoothing. Correspondingly, we can avoid over-smoothing by promoting having bottlenecks that worsen over-squashing.

research_questions.statement: How can we mitigate both over-smoothing and over-squashing simultaneously?

provenance.text_excerpt: We theoretically (Theorem 3) and empirically (Tables 2, 3, and 4) show that both, removing and adding edges is required to find a good compromise in the over-smoothing over-squashing trade-off.

claims.statement: Both edge addition and removal are necessary to find a good compromise in the over-smoothing over-squashing trade-off.

provenance.text_excerpt: JLC is less computationally complex than BFC while keeping the same theoretical properties about the polynomial receptive field growth.

claims.statement: JLC is less computationally complex than BFC while preserving important theoretical properties.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: SJLR outperformed previous methods in homophilous and heterophyllous graph datasets for node classification.

provenance.text_excerpt: SJLR shows the overall best performance in both cases.

claims.statement: SJLR achieves competitive performance, outperforming previous methods in both homophilous and heterophyllous graph datasets for node classification.

claims.statement: SJLR is a critical improvement over SDRF regarding practical adoption of curvature-based methods in GNNs.

methods.name: RDC (Residual/Dense Connections)
methods.protocol_description: Residual or dense skip connections in GNN.

methods.name: FA (Fully-Adjacent layer)
methods.protocol_description: Add fully-adjacent matrix in last GNN layer.

methods.name: SJLR (Stochastic Jost and Liu Curvature Rewiring)
methods.protocol_description: During GNN training, for each layer: compute JLC curvature for all edges; build bank of candidate edges to add from triangles of low-curvature edges; compute improvement scores; drop p_D|E| edges with probability softmax(alpha * phi_d + (1-alpha) * d_norm); add p_A|E| edges from bank with probability softmax(alpha * phi_a - (1-alpha) * a_norm). Graph unchanged at test time. Hyperparameters p_A, p_D, alpha optimized on validation set.

methods.name: SGC (Simple Graph Convolution)
methods.protocol_description: Baseline GNN model with linear graph convolution, no non-linearities between layers.

methods.name: GCN (Graph Convolutional Network)
methods.protocol_description: Standard GCN with ReLU activations and log-softmax output.

methods.name: GDC (Graph Diffusion Convolution)
methods.protocol_description: Preprocessing with personalized PageRank diffusion kernel.

methods.name: SDRF (Stochastic Discrete Ricci Flow)
methods.protocol_description: Curvature-based rewiring using JLC (instead of BFC) as preprocessing.
